newsitem.title: UK: LSI, BBC to develop DTT chip technology.
newsitem.headline: LSI, BBC to develop DTT chip technology.

text.p: U.S. computer chip firm LSI Logic Corp said on Wednesday it has agreed to develop a single-chip digital terrestial television (DTT) solution jointly with the BBC.

"By working together, LSI Logic and the BBC are enabling the deployment of a new European digital broadcast standard, a new market and improved broadcast quality," said LSI chairman and chief executive Wilfred Corrigan in a statement.

LSI said its chip would enable set-top box and TV manufacturers to bring mutliple channel options to all European households in a cost-effective way. First samples of the chip will be available in January, 1998.
DTT is the digital broadcast of television signals from ordinary land-based transmitters to rooftop aerials.

A decoder or TV set with built-in decoder is required to receive the signals but the technology means all homes have potential access to multi-channel television rather than just cable and satellite households.
DTT is set to begin in Britain in mid-1998, with up to 30 television programme services.
The BBC will use the extra capacity to broadcast a number of new channels including a 24-hour news service.
Existing terrestrial broadcasters including the BBC and the ITV network will be joined by new pay television companies offering 15 or so channels.
The ITC is expected to decide in the next few weeks whether to award three key DTT licences to a consortium grouping British television giants Granada, Carlton and BSkyB.
They face competition from NTL Inc, which has secured backing from United News & Media if its bid is successful.
